latest.title: Harness Engineering with Nothing but Markdown
latest.description: Harness engineering isn't just for coding agents. For non-coding business automation agents using MCP tools like Slack and Google Calendar, relying on volatile prompts leads to repeated mistakes. The solution is building a structured, persistent Markdown environment. By setting prohibited actions, mandatory session-end tasks, and forced knowledge checks in instruction files (e.g., Project Knowledge), you make execution rules permanent and reliable, bridging the gap to mechanical linters.

latest.title: What Changes and What Stays the Same for SRE with AWS Frontier Agents
latest.description: AWS GA’d DevOps & Security Agents ("Frontier Agents"). With a 2-month free trial, they automate routine SRE tasks like alert investigations (linking metrics, logs, and code via MCP) and continuous pen-testing ($50/hr). DevOps Agent offers support spend credits but requires human approvals for production fixes. Security Agent automates PR & design reviews. This shifts SRE work: agents handle speed-intensive data correlation, while humans focus on business judgments and architectural decisions.

latest.title: Architecture Layers That S3 Files Eliminates — and Creates
latest.description: AWS S3 Files (GA April 2026) lets you mount S3 buckets as NFS v4.1/4.2 filesystems on EC2, EKS, ECS, and Lambda. Unlike FUSE-based tools, it connects EFS to S3 for real NFS semantics, syncing changes via a 60-second "stage and commit" model. This eliminates S3-to-EBS/EFS staging pipelines, frees Lambda from /tmp limits via lazy hydration, and replaces custom sync setups. It also enables high read throughput up to 3 GiB/s and simplifies file-based AI agent access, though versioning and VPC are required.

latest.title: When Software Development Common Sense Flips: The Law of Decreasing Generation Costs
latest.description: AI coding tools reinvent 20 years of human team practices. As code generation costs plummet, a key law emerges: the center of value shifts from the product to the intent. Traditional tasks like DRY, refactoring, and test coverage flip from absolute rules to situational choices. Conversely, refining intent—verbalizing specs, recording design decisions, and review skills—becomes the ultimate bottleneck. History repeats, and past team failures now reappear in AI workflows.

latest.title: Building TurfArena: A 100% Serverless Operating System for Local Sports Communities
latest.description: Every weekend, thousands of local sports tournaments are organized across India. Amateurs, students, and working professionals flood neighborhood turfs to play football, cricket, basketball, volleyball, and badminton. Yet, if you look under the hood, this booming ecosystem still relies entirely on chaotic WhatsApp groups, manual spreadsheets, paper diaries, and frantic phone calls. We wondered—could cloud technology simplify this entire ecosystem and give grassroots sports a professional digital foundation?

latest.title: Why Kiro Looks Unassuming: Organizing Design Philosophy Differences in the Age of Claude Code and Cursor
latest.description: AI coding tools in 2026 excel in reasoning and autonomy, but Kiro takes a different approach by focusing on "development process state management." While tools like Claude Code and Cursor prioritize speed through parallel agents, Kiro structures premises and specs using Spec (via EARS-format requirements, design, and tasks), Steering (persisting implicit knowledge), and Hooks. Rather than competing on raw reasoning power, Kiro manages context, preventing spec drift and dependency errors in complex projects.

latest.title: Beyond Assistance: The Executive Power of "Agent Plugins for AWS"
latest.description: AWS Labs released "Agent Plugins for AWS" in 2026, an OSS library for Claude Code and Cursor. Unlike standard CLI automation tools that rely on ad-hoc prompts, it adds a structured "AWS Domain Capability" layer over execution. Using Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers like awsknowledge and awspricing, it integrates live data for a 5-step workflow: Analyze, Recommend, Estimate, Generate, and Deploy. This shifts AI's role from design assistance to secure, data-backed execution.

trending.title: AIdeas Finalist: ASET – Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth
trending.description:
ASET (Academic Safety and Evidencing Truth) is a scientific claim verification engine built  for the AI era — where information can be generated instantly, but trust cannot, to address the growing problem of hallucinated citations and  AI-generated information.

Instead of probabilistic prediction, ASET retrieves, analyzes, and synthesizes evidence from 1.2M+ indexed research papers to produce literature-backed verification reports for claims extracted from text, documents, webpages, images, and videos.
